figures.caption: Figure 1: The one-layer autoencoder we consider. n is the input dimension and d is the hidden dimension. ϕ is an activation function acting pointwise. The reconstruction is x′ = x′(x).

Figure 2: Illustration of our results in the case when all the coordinates are i.i.d. and satisfy the strong log-concavity assumption. The solid line is the upper bound min(pdm, d), and the dashed line is the lower bound min(pdm, dp1/m). The gray dotted line is the performance of unsuperposed (orthogonal columns in W ) solutions, i.e., pd. Note that this diagram is purely schematic, since our results hide constants.

Figure 3: Experimental loss curves for d = 10, 15 with m = 3 and n = 6000. We plot numerically optimized values of logd(L̃) v.s. logd(p). Note that at small p the data suggests a linear relationship, as proved by the tight upper and lower bounds above in this case. For larger p, the situation remains ambiguous. The “slope-1/3” lines are drawn such that they satisfy the observed data at p = d−m = d−3.
